diagnosis: The daemon checks persisted session status and queued messages before deleting provider state or image assets.
The mobile deletion path did not await the final session projection save, so a completed turn could be checked against an older busy state.
The old mobile implementation classified explicit delete refusal as unknown and cleared the composer draft before success.
changes: Synchronize the deletion target and await saveTaskState before removeSession; serialize periodic saves and deletion.
Use NIL runtime and a 60-second timeout, longer than the daemon native deletion wait.
Require an ACK before local cleanup; preserve history and draft on failure.
Surface progress and errors above the history drawer; provide a link back to the target session.
Keep unknown outcomes for recovery and do not treat turn completion as deletion confirmation.
automated_coverage: Completed generated image turn with a stale working server projection waits for save acknowledgement before delete.
Actual busy refusal preserves history and draft without an unknown deletion command.
Save or journal failure does not dispatch deletion or leave a permanent sending command.
Timeout, uncertain native reply, malformed acknowledgement and cancellation retain uncertain deletion state.
Unsent retry does not erase earlier uncertainty; terminal turn events resolve controls but not deletion.

passed: Server busy refusal appears over the history drawer with its original reason.
Returning to the target retains the generated image and unsent draft, with no new unknown-result warning.
ACK removes the image conversation; force-stop and restart does not resurrect it.
Request log confirms saveTaskState before removeSession, correct session ID and NIL runtime.
No prompt, start or cancel commands were sent.

limitations: No physical phone or production server deletion was performed.
Genuinely running, queued or unresolved provider tasks remain subject to server deletion guards.
